chunks: And it is narrated from Muṣādif, who said:
I was with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام on land belonging to him while they were harvesting, and a beggar came asking, so I said: “May Allah provide for you.”
So he said: “Hold on. That is not for you, until you give three. Then if you give after that, it is for you, and if you withhold, it is for you.”

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh, Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام
key_terms.سَائِلٌ: a petitioner or beggar asking for assistance
key_terms.مُصَادِفٍ: Muṣādif, the narrator of this report
key_terms.يَصْرِمُونَ: they were harvesting or cutting the produce

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teach about responding to a beggar during the harvest?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that one should not dismiss a petitioner with words alone before first giving a due share from the harvest. It reflects an ethic of responsibility toward the needy, after which further giving becomes optional.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1665 - It is narrated from Musadif, who said:
I was with Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) on his land while they were harvesting. A beggar came asking for something, and I said, "May Allah (swt) provide for you."

The Imam (as) said: "Hold on! That is not for you to say until you have given three times. After you have given three times, if you give more, it is for you (to decide), and if you withhold, it is also for you (to decide)."
